newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EMI chief applauds greater BoE independence.
newsitem.headline: EMI chief applauds greater BoE independence.

text.p: Britain's decision to give the Bank of England greater independence in setting monetary policy was greeted with enthusiasm on Wednesday by Alexandre Lamfalussy, head of the European Monetary Institute.
"It was music to my ears," Lamfalussy told a monetary sub-committee of the European Parliament.
"Maastricht or no Maastricht it's a good thing. I think this is a very major step towards compliance with the treaty's objectives," he added.

The decision on Tuesday by Gordon Brown, Britain's new Chancellor of the Exchequer, to give the Bank of England freedom in setting interest rates does not comply fully with the Maastricht treaty's criterion on central bank independence.
The British Treasury still retains the right to set an inflation target for the Bank, a feature that would have to be scuttled if full compliance was sought.
Lamfalussy said Brown's decision would also imply less volatility in sterling's relations with other European currencies, particularly once a single currency is formed.

Although Britain has rejected the notion of joining a revamped Exchange Rate Mechanism, linking the euro to those not participating in the first wave of entrants, the EMI chief said exchange rate stability was an objective shared by Britain.
"I think the risks of having problems with the UK are substantially diminished," Lamfalussy said.
